findings.reproduction: Open the real workbench against disposable FastAPI, admit a synthetic incident, and close the first SSE response normally.
findings.expected: Stale state disables cancellation until a successful reconnect and snapshot refresh.
findings.observed: Before the change the workbench displayed Live and cancellation stayed enabled.
findings.root_cause: Clean EOF left the prior live state in place during reconnect backoff.
findings.repair: Close the actual stream reader and transition to stale on EOF or read failure. The browser repro and CI-covered transport regressions passed.
acceptance: Chrome keyboard admission, clean EOF, recovery, and a 390 px viewport

findings.reproduction: Invoke the registered investigation activity on a missing source or exhausted probe budget and read the scoped assessment API.
findings.expected: Abstention leaves a typed assessment for the operator.
findings.observed: The activity returned ABSTAINED with an empty assessment list.
findings.root_cause: Early probe failures exited before persisting an assessment.
findings.repair: Store typed failure decisions through the existing assessment ledger and preserve existing immutable decisions on retry.

findings.reproduction: Re-evaluate the registered activity after a successful probe snapshot while the synthetic target is now healthy at the same version.
findings.observed: Initial assessment was PROPOSED even though the downstream paths check current health.
findings.root_cause: The initial decision evaluated the version without checking current target health.
findings.repair: Recheck health while building an assessment and persist the typed reason.

findings.reproduction: Request incident outcome history after seeding 51 synthetic revisions with a final dispute.
findings.expected: The bounded history includes the newest revision.
findings.observed: The oldest-first SQL limit hid revision 51.
findings.root_cause: SQL applied LIMIT to ascending revisions.
findings.repair: Select the latest 50 and serialize them in the same chronological order as before.

findings.reproduction: Submit an ordinary invalid proposal whose strategy value is an array or object.
findings.root_cause: Validation used set membership before ensuring the value was a string.
findings.repair: Validate the type before comparing the allowed strategy names.

findings.reproduction: Run two authenticated registrations against native disposable PostgreSQL with the test barrier holding both manifest inserts.
findings.expected: Both requests return the same frozen manifest and leave one row.
findings.observed: Before the fix, the barrier reproduced HTTP 500 and HTTP 201.
findings.root_cause: A check-then-insert race collided on deterministic identity; both natural and primary keys matter.
findings.repair: Make insertion atomic and retrieve the expected immutable identity. Same-version content drift keeps the original manifest.

findings.reproduction: Begin an UPDATE that invalidates the candidate and attempt HTTP registration before that transaction commits.
findings.expected: Registration waits for the concurrent decision and declines a now-invalid candidate.
findings.observed: The prior read could observe the pre-update candidate and freeze a manifest while invalidation was in progress.
findings.root_cause: The candidate read and manifest insert were not ordered against invalidation's candidate update.
findings.repair: Take a PostgreSQL shared row lock before validating the candidate and freezing the manifest.

findings.reproduction: Call the registered activity in the documented development opt-in with a local counting provider.
findings.expected: Route evidence identifies the approved strategy and the resources it uses.
findings.observed: A RUNBOOK-labelled run invoked the opted-in provider and recorded token use.
findings.root_cause: The development advisory override is outside the versioned route identity.
findings.repair: Pin model and reservation to a separately selected development route. Keep RUNBOOK deterministic and replay settled legacy advice without new spending.

findings.reproduction: Submit reviewer-authenticated outcome correction and failure review through the API and inspect the resulting durable rows.
findings.expected: Corrections and reviews retain their server-authenticated reviewer pseudonym.
findings.observed: The API previously checked the role and discarded the resolved identity.
findings.root_cause: Neither writer persisted the actor that the server had already authenticated.
findings.repair: Persist the server-derived pseudonym for new review records and preserve unknown attribution in historical rows.

findings.reproduction: Open a proposed plan in Chrome, have a competing authorized reviewer reject it first, then submit the stale browser approval.
findings.expected: The conflict is reported and the preview is refreshed from durable plan and approval records.
findings.observed: FastAPI returned 409, but the preview continued to show the previous proposal.
findings.root_cause: The browser refreshed only after successful review writes.
findings.repair: Refetch for successful and conflicting or forbidden decisions, and disable review controls if the preview cannot be refreshed.
acceptance: Chrome against real FastAPI with competing synthetic reviews

findings.reproduction: Observe a verified outcome in a connected workbench, then use the authorized feedback endpoint to dispute it without changing incident projection state.
findings.expected: The workbench refetches the scoped outcome and removes the old verified result.
findings.observed: The outcome transaction wrote a revision without a durable event for connected clients.
findings.root_cause: Independent witness and reviewer dispute writes did not emit workbench notifications.
findings.repair: Commit one scoped UI event alongside each new revision, including when the incident projection version stays unchanged.
acceptance: Chrome against real FastAPI with a synthetic reviewer dispute
